hook: Erik Brynjolfsson is an economist who studies how information technology and AI change productivity, work and the way the economy is measured. After a long career at MIT Sloan, where he directed the Initiative on the Digital Economy, he moved to Stanford in 2020 to lead the new Digital Economy Lab. His books with Andrew McAfee carried that research to a general audience, and his essay The Turing Trap argues for AI that augments people rather than replaces them.
name: Erik Brynjolfsson

quick_facts: Directs the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and is the Jerry Yang and Akiko Yamazaki Professor and a Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, according to the lab's page retrieved in October 2026.

Also a Ralph Landau Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research, professor by courtesy at the Graduate School of Business and in Economics, and a research associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research.
Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in applied mathematics and decision sciences from Harvard and a PhD in managerial economics from MIT.
At MIT he directed the Initiative on the Digital Economy and held the Schussel Family Professorship at the Sloan School before joining Stanford in July 2020.
Co-founded Workhelix with Andrew McAfee, a company that measures where AI investment creates value inside organisations.
Co-chaired, with Tom Mitchell, the National Academies committee behind the consensus report Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work.

achievements.title: The Second Machine Age (2014, with Andrew McAfee)
achievements.impact: A New York Times best-seller that brought the economics of automation and digital technology to a general readership. It followed Race Against the Machine and preceded Machine, Platform, Crowd, both also written with McAfee.

achievements.title: The Productivity J-Curve (2021)
achievements.impact: With Daniel Rock and Chad Syverson, showed that poorly measured intangible investment around general purpose technologies makes productivity growth look slow at first and faster later.

achievements.title: The Turing Trap (2022)
achievements.impact: Argued that market incentives and tax policy push AI toward automating human labor, which weakens workers and concentrates wealth, and called for steering AI toward augmenting people.

achievements.title: Recognition from INFORMS and the University of Turku
achievements.impact: Won the John D.C. Little Best Paper Award in 1999 for work on bundling information goods, was named an Information Systems Society Distinguished Fellow in 2011, and received an honorary doctorate from the University of Turku in 2020.

achievements.title: Founding director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab
achievements.impact: Leads the lab Stanford set up around his arrival in 2020 to study how digital technology and AI affect the economy.
